simple.meaning: בָּלֶה (bâleh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “worn out.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Joshua 9:4. The background is built from the passages where the word occurs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to בָּלֶה (H1087) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: בָּלֶה (bâleh) / H1087 is traced through Joshua 9:4, Joshua 9:5, Ezekiel 23:43 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.full: H1087. baleh [ בָּלֶה ] adjective worn out ; feminine בָּלָה Ezek 23:43 (of a woman, compare Gen 18:12 above); plural בָּלִים Josh 9:4 (sacks), 9:4 (wine-skins), בָּלוֺת 9:5 (sandals), 9:5 (garments).
